tagline.text: Indoor-outdoor amusement park and Snow World at the CCP Complex in Pasay

location.label: Location
location.text: Inside the CCP Complex, Vicente Sotto Street, Barangay 76, Pasay City

best_season.label: Best time to visit
best_season.text: November–May dry season (many indoor rides, so it works year-round)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱849~1,059 (per person, entry plus unlimited ride pass)

children.text: Star City is Manila's best-known amusement park, opened in 1991 inside the CCP Complex in Pasay. After a fire in 2019 it reopened in 2022, and a single pass covers more than 30 rides and attractions plus the indoor Snow World add-on.

Star City is an indoor-outdoor amusement park of about 35,000 square meters inside the Cultural Center of the Philippines (CCP) Complex, built on reclaimed land along Manila Bay. It belongs to Barangay 76 in Pasay City, and Wikipedia (14°33′22″ N, 120°59′09″ E) and OpenStreetMap (about 14.5557, 120.9857) point to the same spot. The operator is Star Parks Corporation, part of the Elizalde Holdings group.

The park grew out of an annual Christmas toy and gift fair that began in 1976, and it opened as an amusement park on February 23, 1991. Before the fire it drew about 1.5 million visitors a year. On October 2, 2019, a major fire destroyed roughly 80% of the main building that housed the rides and also damaged Snow World. The cause is reported to be an electrical fault. After delays caused by COVID-19, it reopened on February 24, 2022, with 25 rides and 6 attractions. According to its current official information, the park has about 30 rides and attractions in total.

The park is split into an indoor main building and an outdoor area. Indoors you will find the air-conditioned Grand Carousel, bumper cars, Time Warp, and the haunted walk-through Gabi ng Lagim, while outside there is the Giant Star Wheel, which carries you high above the grounds, along with thrill rides such as the Star Flyer (which hangs riders upside down), the Star Frisbee and the Surf Dance. Most of the fun happens indoors even on hot days, which makes it a good family option during the rainy season. First-time visitors should understand the ticket structure first. There is no separate entrance fee to speak of, and the all-you-can-ride Star Pass is effectively the standard ticket. The pass price already includes the ₱80 entrance fee, so if you want to ride more than three or four rides, the unlimited pass is the better deal, whether you come alone or with family. A guardian who only accompanies a small child pays just the ₱80 entrance, which is a light cost. With about 30 rides and waiting times that vary by hour, you will be happier choosing your favorites than trying to ride everything in one afternoon.

Note, however, that reports say the land lease expires in 2026 and that the government has been working toward selling the property. No closing date has been announced, but operations could change, so please check the official announcements before you go.
This Ferris wheel has 32 air-conditioned gondolas. Ride it around sunset for a sweeping view of Manila Bay and the CCP Complex. Children at least
86 cm
tall can ride with an adult. The view from the top over the CCP Complex and the bay also makes it a popular spot for family photos.

blocks.title: Star Flyer and the thrill rides

children.text: The Star Flyer, which was introduced when it opened in 2007 as the Philippines' first inverted coaster, along with the Star Frisbee and the Surf Dance, is limited to riders at least
122 cm
tall (48 inches). They are in the outdoor area, which was relatively less damaged in the fire.
A water log flume ride where you float down a channel in a log boat. There is a 48-inch minimum height, and you may get wet, so it helps to bring a change of clothes.

An indoor ice play zone entered with a separate combo ticket. With ice carvings and a snow play area, it offers a different experience in sweltering Manila. Photography is not allowed inside Snow World.

There are many rides for kids, such as the Grand Carousel, Antique Cars, Kiddie Wheel, Mini Pirate Ship and Kids Playland. Most are set up so that children about 30 to 42 inches tall can ride with an adult, which suits trips with toddlers. Because many rides need a guardian aboard, remember that one adult with two children will have to take turns.
A Filipino-style haunted house with entry left to parental discretion. It may be scary for young children, so decide based on your child's temperament.
Seated indoor attractions such as Dinosaur Alive!, the Digital Surround Theater and Time Warp let families who cannot take the rides play together.

items.title: Half-day plan
items.subtitle: Open in the afternoon and finish in the evening

Leave your bags in a locker and start lightly in the indoor main building with the Grand Carousel, the bumper cars and Time Warp.
Move to the outdoor area and ride the thrill rides such as the Star Flyer and the Surf Dance. Rides with long lines are shorter on weekdays.
Before the sun sets, ride the Giant Star Wheel and enjoy the sunset and the view of Manila Bay.
Have dinner at a restaurant in the park, or walk around the CCP Complex after you leave.

items.title: Full-day plan
items.subtitle: Including Snow World with a combo ticket

children.text: Enter with the Star Pass and Snow World combo ticket, and begin with the ice experience in Snow World.
After lunch and a snack, go around the indoor rides, and depending on how you feel, try the Star Frisbee and Jungle Splash.
Finish with the Giant Star Wheel, then head out to the CCP Complex promenade.
Star City is close to central Manila (near Ermita and Malate), so a taxi or Grab from almost anywhere in the city gets you there in about
15 to 40 minutes
(it varies greatly with traffic).
Take LRT-1 and get off at Vito Cruz station, then ride a tricycle for about
10 to 15 minutes
; the fare is reported at around ₱120. The LRT-1 fare is about
depending on the distance.
Ninoy Aquino International Airport (MNL) is about
5 to 7 km
away. Grab or a taxi is the easiest, and it is best to avoid rush hour.
The Blue Bay Walk West parking lot near the CCP Complex is used, and it is reported to cost about
for the first 3 hours. Please confirm parking rates on site.
Roads nearby can be closed during events, so please check the latest traffic notices before you travel.
With so many indoor rides you can go year-round, but the dry season is better for the outdoor rides and the Ferris wheel. Expect crowds during school vacations, holidays and the year-end season.

The park only operates Thursday through Sunday, so weekdays (Thursday and Friday) tend to have shorter lines, though holidays can be busy. The park sometimes closes temporarily for national events or road closures, so check the announcements after you pick a date.

Inside the park there are food outlets such as Sizzling Grill, Tropicana Hut, a Korean snack place and a Chinese restaurant. Outside food and drinks are not allowed, except baby milk and baby food. It is safest to buy water inside.

Many visitors stay in hotels around Ermita and Malate, near the CCP Complex, or in the Pasay area close to City of Dreams Manila. If you plan to stay until evening, lodging close to the park makes getting back easier.

Many Korean travelers eat elsewhere before going in. Food in the park may cost more than in the city, so one option is to have a meal at a restaurant near the CCP Complex or in Malate or Ermita before entering. Please check at the gate whether you can leave and re-enter.

Vouchers from online sellers must be exchanged for a physical ticket at the counter at the entrance. Have your QR code or voucher ready in advance.
Senior citizens and persons with disabilities are advised to get 20% off at the gate with a valid ID, though this may not be combined with online discounts.
Many rides have height limits, so measure your children beforehand; the thrill rides are only for those at least 122 cm tall.
Wearing socks is best in Snow World, and photos are not allowed inside. Closed shoes such as sneakers are recommended.
Payment by cash, card, GCash and Maya is reported to be accepted. Token games are not included in the unlimited pass.
If you plan to ride Jungle Splash, bring a towel and a change of clothes.
Because the park opens in the afternoon and runs into the night, do not combine it with a daytime plan; a good order is to see Malate and Intramuros in the morning and enter in the afternoon.
Families with children can rent wheelchairs, strollers and mobility scooters on site, so ask at the entrance if you need one.
Online prices change by date, and coupons often cannot be combined with gate discounts. Compare both before you go.

Star City was announced to be temporarily closed on November 7~18, 2026, because of road closures for the ASEAN summit, and the land lease ends in 2026 with sale discussions underway. Be sure to confirm that the park is operating before you visit.
Operating hours can change and rides can stop because of weather, safety or capacity, and no refund may be given in that case.
Pets are not allowed, and smoking is permitted only in designated outdoor areas.
Flying drones over the CCP Complex is prohibited.
Roads around the park may be closed during events, which can greatly increase travel time.
Leave valuables in a locker and keep an eye on your children.
